description: SNAP, the Severe Nuclear Accident Programme, is a Lagrangian atmospheric dispersion model maintained by the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. It represents movement and deposition of radioactive material after a configured release. Users supply release timing and material, gridded meteorological fields in NetCDF and simulation settings; outputs are pollutant trajectories and deposition or concentration fields over the chosen domain and period. Geographic coverage depends on the weather grid. GPL-3.0 source, build instructions, example settings and tagged releases are public. A limitation is that results depend strongly on weather forcing and source-term uncertainty; an illustrative run is not an emergency decision forecast without operational checks. SNAP can support nuclear-facility emergency exercises and infrastructure exposure analysis. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis is a distinct possible historical meteorological source, not necessarily in the model's required vertical format. No meteorological input, model build or release archive was downloaded.
